newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Three Gorges project secures HK investment.
newsitem.headline: China's Three Gorges project secures HK investment.

text.p: Chinese companies involved in developing the Three Gorges Dam project and related facilities secured US$592.7 million in foreign investment during an investment seminar, a Chinese official said on Thursday.

"We have signed contracts and agreement worth a total of US$1.01 billion with foreign firms, of which US$592.7 million will be provided by the foreign side," said Sun Zhigang, mayor of Yichang city in Hubei province.
Yichang sits just southeast and down river from the Three Gorges hydroelectric project in Hubei province.
Sun led a group from the city of Yichang to the Hubei Investment and Trade Promotion Seminar in Hong Kong.

Yichang has been designated an open city by Beijing and is permitted to encourage foreign trade and investment and offer preferential investment incentives, including tax holidays and preferential tax rates, similar to the coastal cities.
Sun said Yichang had secured seven contracts and six agreements in all, ten of which were with Hong Kong companies.
Trade between Hong Kong and Yichang totalled more than HK$1 billion a year and more than 400 Hong Kong companies have invested in the city.
Its largest agreement was signed with Spar of Canada, a US$392.85 million deal to build a fertilizer plant.
